column8: Mom, the rain is coming in through the kitchen window.
Dad, my stomach hurts after I ate that green mango.
Mom, can I take the leftover rice to school tomorrow?
Dad, the teacher said I talked through the whole lesson.
Mom, I can't find my other sandal under the bed.
Dad, the dog followed me all the way from the lane.
Mom, the power went out and I can't finish my reading.
Dad, may I sleep at Grandma's house tonight?
Mom, I spilled the fish sauce all over my white shirt.
Dad, the neighbor's rooster woke me before sunrise again.
Mom, I don't want this new shirt. The collar itches.
Dad, I saw a snake near the well just now.
Mom, can you tie my hair before we walk to the market?
Dad, I finished the water jug and I'm still thirsty.
Mom, the baby is crying in the hammock and won't stop.
Dad, my bicycle chain came off on the way home.
Mom, I don't understand the homework on page twelve.
Dad, can you come to the school meeting tomorrow morning?
Mom, I gave my lunch to the boy who didn't bring any.
Dad, I'm scared of the thunder. Can I sit with you?
Mom, the ferry man said we missed the last boat.
Dad, I found a coin under the wooden bed.
Mom, my knee is bleeding from when I fell on the path.
Dad, please don't tell Mom I climbed the mango tree.
Wash your hands before you touch the rice, dear.
Put your schoolbag by the door so you don't forget it.
You have a fever. Stay on the mat and I'll get a cool cloth.
I called you three times. Why didn't you answer?
Hold my hand. The market road is full of motorbikes.
You read that page by yourself. I'm glad.
The lamp is low. Close your eyes. I'll stay until you sleep.
Don't run with the knife. Put it back on the tray.
Your uniform is still wet. Wear the old one today.
Stay away from the riverbank. The current is fast today.
I saved you the sweet coconut. Eat it before it melts.
Help me carry this sack of rice into the house.
I know you're tired. Sit down and drink some water first.
If you get lost, stay where you are and call my name.
You left the gate open and the chickens got out.
Wake up. The sun is already over the roof.
Tell the doctor exactly where it hurts. Don't be shy.
Turn the radio down. Grandma is resting.
I packed an extra mango for you. Don't eat it on the bus.
Come inside. The mosquitoes are thick tonight.
Brother, my sandal strap broke. Can you fix it?
Sis, Mom asked where you went after school.
Brother, can I ride on the back of your motorbike?
Sis, I saved you the last piece of grilled fish.
Brother, you used my notebook and didn't put it back.
Sis, the kettle is boiling over. What should I do?
Brother, I got the same score as you on the test.
Sis, can you ask the price? I'm too shy to start.
Brother, I heard something on the roof. Come look.
Sis, the other girls laughed at my old bag.
Brother, will you walk me to the bus stop?
Sis, you hummed that song all morning.
Brother, Dad is looking for the missing wrench.
Sis, I mended the tear in your skirt.
Brother, the buffalo won't move. Can you come?
Sis, may I wear your hair clip to the wedding?
Tie your shoes. We're leaving for school in five minutes.
I'll comb your hair. Hold still for a moment.
If you feel dizzy, sit down and tell me. Don't hide it.
Stir the soup slowly so it doesn't stick.
You hid my keys in the rice jar again, didn't you?
Fold the blankets before Mom gets back from the market.
You spelled that word right. Do the next one the same way.
Stay on this side of the road. I'll hold the lamp.
I asked you not to touch my tools. Put them back.
Blow on the porridge. It's still too hot for you.
I'll take the blame with Dad. You tell the truth next time.
The letter came. You were accepted into the new class.
Carry the small basket. I'll take the heavy one.
Don't answer the door unless you know the voice.
I'm home late. There's rice under the lid. Eat first.
Water the herbs by the fence, then you can play.
Grandma, the jasmine by the steps is blooming.
Grandpa, I brought you the newspaper from the shop.
Grandma, you forgot your glasses on the porch.
Grandpa, may I learn how you tie the fishing net?
Grandma, your soup smells like lemongrass today.
Grandpa, does your knee still hurt when it rains?
Grandma, I'll fan you. The afternoon is heavy.
Grandpa, which stall sells the dried fish you like?
Grandma, I can thread the needle if your eyes are tired.
Grandpa, I caught a small fish. Do you want to see it?
Grandma, hold my arm on the pagoda steps.
Grandpa, you left the kettle on the stove.
